happened: Congress did not repeal the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act or the Inflation Reduction Act. The July 4, 2025 reconciliation law cut back many Inflation Reduction Act tax credits and took back the unspent money in several of its Energy Department loan and grant programs, including loan subsidies, transmission programs and industrial grants. The Energy Department also cancelled 24 large awards worth about $3.7 billion in May 2025 and 321 more worth about $7.6 billion in October 2025.

legal: On January 12, 2026, Judge Amit Mehta of the U.S. District Court for D.C. ruled that DOE's cancellation of seven awards violated equal protection because it was based on how recipients' states voted, and set those terminations aside. The ruling did not cover the other cancelled awards.
closeness: Smaller than full repeal. Both laws remain, and many credits for nuclear, geothermal and batteries continue for longer. The law rescinded unspent money in about nine IRA energy accounts (sections 50123, 50141, 50142, 50144, 50145, 50151-50153 and 50161), not all unspent funds. See ch12-071.
uncertain: How much money the rescissions removed in dollars was not confirmed. Whether the government appealed the January 2026 ruling was not found. Newest source is from October 2026.
